hypothesis: Upgrading the FM to a DeepFM (add a 1-hidden-layer MLP over the concatenated field embeddings) and feeding it standardized past-only numerical priors (user/video/author long_view & click rates plus user×tab historical rate) gives the model new, genuinely predictive signal beyond raw id crosses, since these levers were independently validated as the three largest measured wins in this project's history (+0.0078, +0.0037, +0.0035 stacked to 0.6563 from an FM baseline).
change_spec: 1. In FM class (or a new DeepFM class), after computing the per-field embedding tensor E (B,F,k) as today, ALSO build a numerical feature vector Z (B,M) per row with M=7 past-only fields: (a) user_long_view_rate, (b) user_click_rate, (c) video_long_view_rate, (d) video_click_rate, (e) author_long_view_rate, (f) author_click_rate, (g) user_tab_long_view_rate. 2. Past-only computation rule (must not leak): for TRAIN rows, sort by date, then for each (user|video|author|user,tab) group compute an EXPANDING count and expanding positive-count using only STRICTLY EARLIER-dated rows in train (use cumulative sums indexed by sorted date, subtract same-day rows entirely -- i.e. only rows with date < this row's date count); rate = expanding_pos/expanding_count if expanding_count>0 else the global train long_view rate (0.3366) / click rate fallback. For VALID (and TEST) rows, use the FULL train-split aggregate (all 13 train dates) per group, since validation is strictly after train in time — no expanding computation needed there. 3. Standardize each of the 7 numerical columns using TRAIN-computed mean/std (subtract mean, divide by std, clip to [-5,5]) — fit these stats only on the train rows' computed values. 4. Model: concatenate flatten(E) (F*K) with Z (7 dims) -> Dense(128, relu) -> Dense(1) as `mlp_out`; final logit = FM's existing bias+linear+2nd-order term + mlp_out (DeepFM sum, exactly as Guo et al. 2017). Initialize MLP weights with small random normal (std 0.01), implement forward/backward manually in numpy (matrix multiplies + relu, Adam updates identical style to existing V/W optimizer) — no torch needed. 5. Keep everything else identical: BCE loss, Adam lr=1e-3, batch 8192, K=16, patience 4, max 40 epochs, early stop on validation primary. 6. Runtime: fit 3 variants sequentially in one pipeline run — (a) champion_equiv: plain FM, no MLP, no Z (identical to it00 code path), (b) deepfm_only: MLP added but Z zeroed out (only embeddings), (c) full: MLP + Z as specified. Each fit ~40 epochs x ~3s/epoch (MLP overhead) ≈ 120s, total for 3 variants ≈ 400-500s, well within the 1500s limit. Print `ABLATION champion_equiv primary=...`, `ABLATION deepfm_only primary=...`, `ABLATION full primary=...` after each fit; write the `full` variant's predictions for the requested split as the final pipeline output. 7. Assert only train-side quantities: after building Z, print the vocabulary/group sizes (num users, videos, authors with train history) and print train-side numeric feature means/stds (no assertion on validation metric values). 8. Do not change the CLI, output format, or the train-only constraint; the label (long_view/is_click) must never enter Z for the SAME row being scored — only aggregates from strictly earlier train dates (train) or the full train window (valid/test).
rationale: Per DeepFM (Guo et al., IJCAI 2017), combining a shallow FM component with a deep MLP over the same embeddings lets the model learn arbitrary higher-order interactions without manual feature crossing, addressing the organizers' observation that raw FM capacity is not the bottleneck (§4) — the MLP earns its place here specifically because it is the mechanism that lets the model consume the new past-only numerical priors, not because of added depth alone (§8.5, §2b of the strategy). The numerical features are past-only aggregates of `long_view`/`is_click` per user/video/author/user-tab, which are user×item or item-side interactions (not user-constant terms), so they survive the within-user no-op rule (§2) and were independently the two next-largest wins in this project's ledger. All three levers were measured positive (not merely hypothesized) on this exact dataset in prior runs, satisfying the 'stack every validated rider' rule.
gain_evidence: This project's own ledger (prior runs, same task) measured DeepFM MLP-over-embeddings alone at +0.0078 promoted, then standardized numeric behavioral-rate features at +0.0037, then user-tab historical rates at +0.0035, stacking an FM baseline of 0.6015 up to 0.6563 — the single largest validated levers on this exact split. Combining all three in one iteration (rather than stacking across 3 iterations) should recover most of that combined effect since they are largely additive (MLP supplies capacity to consume the numeric signal; numeric signal supplies genuinely new past-only information the pure-id FM lacks). I discount to +0.009 (well under the naive sum of ~0.015) for engineering risk of the manual-numpy MLP backward pass and to stay defensible under the calibration warning to predict smaller than raw digest sums.
ablation_plan: champion_equiv: FM only (no MLP, no numerical features) — reproduces it00 exactly, sanity check the harness's own baseline reproduction. deepfm_only: MLP added over embeddings but numerical feature vector Z zeroed, isolating the architecture's contribution. full: MLP + all 7 past-only numeric features, the proposed champion.
search_check: I searched arXiv for DeepFM/numerical-feature-embedding work from the last 12 months to see if a newer variant supersedes the plain concat-MLP approach (found AutoDis/embedding-learning-for-numerical-features, Guo et al. 2020/2021, and the original DeepFM 2017 paper); nothing from the last 12 months changes the risk profile of a straightforward DeepFM-with-standardized-numeric-features design, because this iteration is reproducing and consolidating THIS project's own already-measured winning levers (ledger deltas +0.0078/+0.0037/+0.0035), not exploring a new untested architecture family — the evidence justifying the approach is my own prior-run measurements, not literature novelty.
